claims.claim: The Act asks only that a member be Muslim and a citizen

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: The Act asks only that a member be Muslim and a citizen.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: Section 6(2) contains those two positive qualifications, but s.6(3) also contains bankruptcy, criminal-conviction and incapacity disqualifications. The defensible governance point is that the Act lacked specific competence and expertise criteria.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: The impairment charge shrank from RM1,313 million to RM1 million.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: The report compares impairment effects under successive policies and says the final policy enabled RM1 million to be recorded. The sentence can imply that RM1.313 billion was actually booked and then reversed.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: On page 199 the commission asked that its report be made public.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: The actual wording says the commission hoped the government would consider making public whichever parts were suitable. It is neither an unqualified request nor a recommendation to publish the entire report.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: Putrajaya sealed it for almost four years, citing depositor panic. Those it protected were those kept in the dark.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: The dates and Anwar's stated panic rationale are supportable, but 'sealed' collapses classification and successive non-publication into a loaded action by a single actor, while the final sentence presents an untestable causal judgment as fact.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: A bank rewrites its bad-loan rule twice in a year, pays a dividend on the result, then locks the inspector's report away so customers will not worry.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: Tabung Haji is a statutory body, not a bank; the policy concerned investment impairment and included a duration criterion; and the report's publication wording was narrower than the analogy suggests. The analogy compounds several simplifications into a stronger narrative.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: The gate held every year; the number fed into it did not.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: The commission did not find that the legal gate successfully held; it found that the presentation made s.22(3)(a) appear satisfied and that the 2014-2017 distributions contravened s.22. The metaphor also omits the other statutory conditions.

source_assessment: The source list names 14 labeled items: five P-items and nine S-items, although some P-items are statements accessed through the same news stories and therefore are not independent publications. The analysis has a strong documentary core: the RCI report, Act 535, Tabung Haji statements and UJSB's stated transaction figures. It includes a meaningful countervoice from the former Auditor-General and acknowledges Tabung Haji's defense of the restructuring. Its source range extends to government, a statutory body, a government-owned rescue vehicle, Parliament, a former audit official, civil society and several Malaysian newsrooms. However, the cards remain dominated by the RCI and government-linked institutions; they lack an independent accounting-standard expert, depositor or community voice, academic analysis, and a developed opposition response. Some supposedly primary items are reached through news reports, source dates are misstated, and the cited Act reprint is updated only to 2011. The RM2.75 billion contradiction and Madinah's 4 September denial show that the source review was incomplete.
overall_assessment: The central financial finding is reliable: the RCI's detailed tables support RM3.412 billion reported profit, RM1.433 billion MFRS-adjusted loss, a RM3.324 billion 2017 distribution, the impairment-policy changes and the post-distribution deficit series. Most governance and recovery figures also trace correctly to the report. Publication is not safe without revisions, however. The draft overstates s.6 eligibility, omits part of the impairment test, turns modeled impairment effects into a shrinking booked charge, exaggerates the commission's limited publication language, simplifies s.22 into a single gate, and uses an analogy that misdescribes both the institution and the assets. Its provenance also contains two clear errors: RM2.75 billion does appear in the RCI executive summary, and the former minister had not been released as of 4 September. Correct those points, disclose the report's internal RM2.75 billion versus RM3.324 billion inconsistency, preserve attribution to the RCI and institutional speakers, and date-stamp all live legal and enforcement claims.
